newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs end mixed, pork bellies up sharply.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs end mixed, pork bellies up sharply.

text.p: A mixed trend prevailed in CME lean hog futures going into the close with nearbys up on expected cash market strength next week while pork bellies finished sharply higher following the strength in cash bellies, traders said.

Hog futures closed 0.425 cent per lb higher to 0.850 lower with August up 0.250 at 82.175 cents. Pork bellies finished mostly 1.300 to 2.050 cent a lb higher with August up 1.800 at 88.000 cents. May and July posted new contract highs.
Expectations cash hog prices will trend higher next week supported nearby hog futures in light trade, they said.

Packers are expected to show increased demand for hogs after planned light kills this weekend. Firmer cash pork values should prompt stepped-up packer competition for hogs next week, floor sources said.
The market was also technically firm, but did run into chart resistance between 75.000 and 76.500 cents, basis October, they said.
Japan's news that it will exempt some pork imports from tariffs during August and continued speculation that the tariff suspension could last beyond August also bolstered futures, sources said.

A Japanese supermarket chain said it will cut retail prices of imported pork by up to 15 percent during August to match the government's tariff removal on pork imports. This increased the speculation Japan would lift the tariff for longer than one month, market sources said.

R.J. O'Brien, Rand Financials, ING and E.D.&F. Man notably bought while Cargill Investor Services and ABN Chicogo Corp sold. Scattered selling pressured many back months to days lows. In hog options, Smith Barney sold October 76 calls, pit sources said.
Gains in pork bellies were reinforced by reports of stepped-up slicer interest for frozen product and higher fresh belly prices. Buy stops were touched off in February at the close, traders said.
They cited talk that upwards of 114 loads of frozen product had been sold to slicers. Fresh product was also selling at highest levels in over one week, they added.
USDA, in its midday carlot pork report, quoted fresh bellies $1.00 to $2.00 higher, with 14 to 16-lb supplies selling at $92.00 per cwt.

Prudential Securities turned a seller late in August bellies but mixed demand kept that month strong. R.J. O'Brien bought February and Refco sold for buying by E.D.&F. Man pushed that month up into buy stops, pit sources said.
